summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with end-stage renal disease, hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy, and atrial fibrillation was admitted after developing hypotension and atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response during hemodialysis. She was asymptomatic upon arrival, with resolution of both hypotension and arrhythmia. Troponin levels rose during the stay but were attributed to chronic cardiac strain in the setting of ESRD rather than acute infarction. A chest X-ray showed no acute cardiopulmonary process. The patient declined further cardiac interventions after discussion. Her warfarin was held due to a supratherapeutic INR, and lisinopril was discontinued to reduce hypotension risk post-dialysis. She remained stable, expressed a preference to return home, and was discharged on adjusted medications with follow-up plans.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Diabetes with peripheral circulatory disorders, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Peripheral angiopathy in diseases classified elsewhere
